entries.contribution: Can connect New Contextualism to evidence-based urban research, landscape systems, water-sensitive planning and the relationship between ecological infrastructure and everyday urban life. Her writing on canals provides a strong entry point for policy discussion around urban waterways, public space and environmental justice.

Can bring a gender-sensitive and care-centred perspective to the Practice & Policy Council. Her project demonstrates how spatial design can respond to vulnerability, wellbeing, dignity and access to supportive environments, extending contextual practice beyond physical setting to include social realities and lived experience.

Can strengthen the council’s community engagement and spatial-justice agenda. Her practice foregrounds listening, co-design and the agency of women, young people and marginalised communities. This is central to a contextual approach that treats local people as participants in shaping space, rather than passive recipients of design.

In this council, he can help translate academic principles into professional design methods and urban interventions, ensuring that contextual research is tested against implementation, technical constraints, mobility needs and the everyday performance of places.

Can contribute to heritage conservation and place-based urban regeneration. Her work demonstrates how cultural memory can be translated into connected public spaces, local economic activity and a living heritage trail, rather than treating heritage as an isolated monument.

Can advance the council’s work on adaptive reuse, industrial heritage and regenerative urban development. Her project offers a concrete example of connecting historic production landscapes with contemporary community needs, economic continuity and ecological resilience through a New Contextualism lens.
